sources.entry: C: _Sol - An MQTT broker from scratch_

summary.title: MQTT broker from scratch #1 - The protocol
summary.one_liner: You learn how to model MQTT 3.1.1 control packets (fixed header, CONNECT, PUBLISH, SUBSCRIBE and ACKs) as C structs and unions, and how to pack and unpack them from bytes.
takeaways: MQTT packets consist of a fixed header, an optional variable header and an optional payload.
The Remaining Length field uses a variable-length encoding with a continuation bit, at most four bytes.
C unions with bitfields can map individual bits of the MQTT header byte (type, flags, QoS, retain).
Pack and unpack helpers use network byte order (htons/ntohs) to serialize big-endian fields.
The series builds a minimal single-threaded, epoll-based MQTT 3.1.1 broker in C for Linux.
summary.summary: This first post of the 'Sol' series designs the protocol layer of a minimal MQTT 3.1.1 broker written in C for Linux. It explains the MQTT fixed header, the remaining-length encoding, and the CONNECT, PUBLISH and SUBSCRIBE packet layouts, then shows the corresponding C header and implementation code (mqtt.h, mqtt.c, pack.h, pack.c). The author describes the planned series of six parts plus a multithreading bonus, with the broker intended as an MVP and a learning project.
